defs.en: To perceive the truth or factuality of; to be certain of; to be certain that.
defs.ex: I know that I’m right and you’re wrong.

defs.en: To be or become aware or cognizant.
defs.ex: Did you know Michelle and Jack were getting divorced? ― Yes, I knew.

defs.en: To be aware of; to be cognizant of.
defs.ex: Did you know Michelle and Jack were getting divorced? ― Yes, I knew.

defs.en: To be acquainted or familiar with; to have encountered.
defs.ex: I know your mother, but I've never met your father.

defs.en: To experience.
defs.ex: Their relationship knew ups and downs.

ja: （人）と知り合いである、面識がある
詳しく知る。できる能力がある。上手にできる。
見分ける。また、同定する。

defs.en: Knowledge; the state of knowing. (Now confined to the fixed phrase in the know.)
Used at the end of a sentence to draw attention to information one thinks the listener should keep in mind.
defs.ex: Make sure you water the plants, know…

defs.en: Synonym of you know (used as a conversational discourse marker, to emphasize something)
To continue in (a course or mode of action); to not intermit or fall from; to uphold or maintain.
defs.ex: to keep silence; to keep possession

defs.en: To remain faithful to a given promise or word.
defs.ex: to keep one's word; to keep one's promise

defs.en: To maintain possession of.
defs.ex: I keep a small stock of painkillers for emergencies.

defs.en: To maintain the condition of; to preserve in a certain state.
defs.ex: I keep my specimens under glass to protect them.

defs.en: To record transactions, accounts, or events in.
defs.ex: I used to keep a diary.

defs.en: The main tower of a castle or fortress, located within the castle walls.
The food or money required to keep someone alive and healthy; one's support, maintenance.
defs.ex: He works as a cobbler's apprentice for his keep.

defs.en: The state of being kept; hence, the resulting condition; case.
defs.ex: to be in good keep

defs.en: A cap for holding something, such as a journal box, in place.
A type, race or category; a group of entities that have common characteristics such that they may be grouped together.
defs.ex: What kind of (a) person are you?

defs.en: A makeshift or otherwise atypical specimen.
defs.ex: The opening served as a kind of window.

defs.en: Goods or services used as payment, as e.g. in barter.
defs.ex: in kind

defs.en: Equivalent means used as response to an action.
defs.ex: in kind

defs.en: Each of the two elements of the communion service, bread and wine.
Having a benevolent, courteous, friendly, generous, gentle, liberal, sympathetic, or warm-hearted nature or disposition, marked by consideration for – and service to – others.
Affectionate.
defs.ex: a kind man; a kind heart

defs.en: Favorable.
Mild, gentle, forgiving
defs.ex: The years have been kind to Richard Gere; he ages well.

defs.en: Gentle; tractable; easily governed.
defs.ex: a horse kind in harness

defs.en: Identified as a specific type; famous, renowned.
defs.ex: He was a known pickpocket.

defs.en: Accepted, familiar, researched.
defs.ex: At the time, Einstein's theory was unknown to most other scientists.

defs.en: Any fact or situation which is known or familiar.
defs.ex: You have to tell the knowns from the unknowns.

defs.en: A constant or variable the value of which is already determined.
Deoxidized.
Inactivated.
A male monarch; a man who heads a monarchy; in an absolute monarchy, the supreme ruler of his nation.
defs.ex: Henry VIII was the king of England from 1509 to 1547.

defs.en: The monarch with the most power and authority in a monarchy, regardless of sex.
A male leader of a traditional Aboriginal group, often used as a title by colonists.
A powerful or majorly influential person; someone who holds the preeminent position.
defs.ex: Howard Stern styled himself as the "king of all media".

defs.en: Something that has a preeminent position.
defs.ex: In times of financial panic, cash is king.

defs.en: To crown king, to make (a person) king.
To rule over as king.
To perform the duties of a king.
To assume or pretend preeminence (over); to lord it over.
To promote a piece of draughts/checkers that has traversed the board to the opposite side, that piece subsequently being permitted to move backwards as well as forwards.
An object designed to open and close a lock or to activate or deactivate something, especially a length of metal inserted into a narrow opening on the lock to which it is matched (keyed).
defs.ex: This key is to the backdoor.

defs.en: A card or fob that electronically signals a lock to open.
defs.ex: My hotel room key is a card.

defs.en: A piece of information (e.g., a password or passphrase) used to encode or decode a message or messages.
A password restricting access to an IRC channel.
A key bump (A portion of a recreational drug in powdered form that is snorted from a key or similar small object.)
defs.ex: I saw him snort a key at the party.

ja: （問題解決などの）鍵。手掛かり。秘訣。
（コンピュータ、タイプライターなどの）鍵。キー。

defs.en: Indispensable, supremely important.
defs.ex: He is the key player on his soccer team.

defs.en: Important, salient.
defs.ex: She makes several key points.

ja: 必須の。主要な。肝要な。重要な。

defs.en: To fit (a lock) with a key.
To fit (pieces of a mechanical assembly) with a key to maintain the orientation between them.
To mark or indicate with a symbol indicating membership in a class.
To depress (a telegraph key).
To operate (the transmitter switch of a two-way radio).

ja: （キーで）入力する。タイプする。

defs.en: To put to death; to extinguish the life of.
defs.ex: Smoking kills more people each year than alcohol and hard drugs combined.

defs.en: To render inoperative.
defs.ex: He killed the engine and turned off the headlights, but remained in the car, waiting.

defs.en: To stop, cease, or render void; to terminate.
defs.ex: The editor decided to kill the story.

defs.en: To amaze, exceed, stun, or otherwise incapacitate.
defs.ex: That night, she was dressed to kill.

defs.en: To cause great pain, discomfort, or distress to; to hurt.
defs.ex: These tight shoes are killing my feet.

ja: （受動態で、事故・戦争などにより）死ぬ。

defs.en: The act of killing.
defs.ex: The assassin liked to make a clean kill, and thus favored small arms over explosives.

defs.en: Specifically, the death blow.
defs.ex: The hunter delivered the kill with a pistol shot to the head.

defs.en: The result of killing; that which has been killed.
defs.ex: The fox dragged its kill back to its den.

defs.en: An instance of killing; a score on the tally of enemy personnel or vehicles killed or destroyed.
defs.ex: confirmed kills

defs.en: The grounding of the ball on the opponent's court, winning the rally.
All persons, singular and plural, present form of know.
defs.ex: I knows just what they knows.

defs.en: A child, adolescent, or (loosely) a young adult.
defs.ex: She's a kid. It's normal for her to have imaginary friends.

defs.en: A person whose childhood took place in a particular time period or area.
defs.ex: Only '90s kids will remember this toy.

defs.en: One's son or daughter, regardless of age.
defs.ex: This is Bobby, he is our youngest kid.

defs.en: Used as a form of address for a child, teenager or young adult.
An inexperienced person or one in a junior position.
To dupe or deceive.
defs.ex: Are you kidding me?

defs.en: To deceive or dupe as a joke.
defs.ex: Stop kidding me! It's not funny.

defs.en: To deceive oneself by having unrealistic expectations.
defs.ex: You're kidding yourself if you think you can be a rockstar.

defs.en: To mock or make a fool of (someone) in a playful way.
defs.ex: They were always kidding her for her stutter.

defs.en: To joke.
defs.ex: You must be kidding!
